$schema-note: Catalogo dei server MCP: template, spenti finché la persona non li accende (un account del servizio in accounts.json per quelli con _service, _profiles nel suo servers.json per gli altri: qui scrivono _profiles []). I server propri vanno solo nel servers.json della persona, mai qui. Dopo una modifica il launcher ricostruisce la config da solo al prossimo avvio (`agents mcp sync` lo fa subito, senza chiudere Claude). Campi: _profiles (default: TUTTI i profili dichiarati in profiles/*/profile.json), _surfaces (cli|desktop, default cli). Nessun elenco di profili qui: si deriva dai manifest. _service: il server è legato agli account di quel servizio (shared/mcp/accounts.json): la config di avvio lo dà solo ai profili che ne vedono almeno uno, gli passa AGENTS_MULTI_PROFILE e sostituisce {hosts} con gli host di quegli account (per --allow-net). I secret stanno nel vault, mai qui.

syncthing-status._note: A template, off by default: turn it on in your servers.json with _profiles (the profiles that see it, or null for every one). Reads the local Syncthing (127.0.0.1:8384) with the API key of its config.xml.

n8n._note: n8n-mcp (czlonkowski, MIT), one server per n8n account: n8n-<account>. No deletions: switched off in the server (DISABLED_TOOLS / DISABLED_TOOL_OPERATIONS, the package's own list of destructive operations) and denied in the settings; credentials are not exposed at all (their reads carry secrets). An update to an active workflow republishes it (the package sends no publishIfActive=false): updates and test runs ask first. CLI only: node comes from nvm, which Desktop's bare PATH does not have. Installed by `agents install` at the version in _npm (tools/mcp), started with node: no npx parent process. The version is pinned there: raise it on purpose. Reading a workflow asks too: n8n-mcp returns its nodes as they are, and keys written into a node's parameters instead of a credential come back in clear (13 workflows on one account, audit of 2026-10-05). Telemetry is off (N8N_MCP_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: the package sends sanitised workflows to its author by default), and so are its result cards, which only cost context here.

tasks._note: Le task stanno nel brain (shared/mcp/lib/brain-tasks.ts): _service brain dà l'host e il profilo, il token personale sta nel vault (brain/brain). ~/brains/tasks resta per settings.json e i file allegati dalla console. Un profilo di lavoro (brainScope nel manifest) riceve AGENTS_MULTI_BRAIN_SCOPE e vede solo le task di quei progetti.

agents._note: The hub's children for a coordinator (shared/mcp/lib/agents.ts): sessions of any profile at work in a project, every permission they need answered by the owner. No profile by default: a person's servers.json names the coordinator's (_profiles). Starting a child of another profile uses that profile's account. agent_answer and workflow_answer are in no list on purpose: they answer a child's permission request, which the owner decides first (AskUserQuestion); the permission mode judges the call, and the same for agent_adopt and workflow_adopt (taking an orphan: only when the owner wants it carried on). routine_add, routine_rm and routine_run schedule unattended work: also left to the permission mode.

brain._note: The person's brain (apps/brain/), at the address of their brain account in accounts.json. For the profiles that do not have it as the claude.ai connector "Brain" (their servers.json chooses which, with _profiles): sign in once per profile with /mcp (passphrase + TOTP), the token stays on that machine. CLI only (http). Everything runs unasked but deleting a page and clearing the inbox: every change is in the page's history (brain_restore).

cloudflare._note: Cloudflare's official MCP (Code Mode: docs, search, execute — execute runs JavaScript against the whole API), one server per Cloudflare account token: cloudflare-<account>. It cannot switch deletions off and masks nothing: shared/hooks/cloudflare-guard.ts reads the code of every execute — reads pass, any DELETE is denied, writes ask. It stops mistakes, not code written to slip past it: the token (broad, but no members, tokens or account settings) stays the hard boundary. An account token also needs Account Settings: Read, to find its account. Workers are built and deployed with wrangler, on the same token: agents vault run cloudflare -- wrangler … (apps/cli/toolrun.ts). CLI only (http).

supabase._note: Supabase's official MCP (the npm package, the same tools as mcp.supabase.com), one server per Supabase login: supabase-<account>, with that login's personal access token. Unbound it sees every org and project of the login. A project ties it to itself in .claude/claude-multi.json (git-ignored everywhere by install): {"supabase": {"project": "<ref>", "readOnly": true|false}} — then it reaches that project only, and the account tools (list_projects…) are gone. Deletions of branches (and their data) are denied; pausing a project is reversible and stays. CLI only: node comes from nvm, which Desktop's bare PATH does not have. Installed by `agents install` at the version in _npm (tools/mcp), started with node: no npx parent process. The version is pinned there: raise it on purpose.

lovable._note: Lovable's official MCP, one server per Lovable account: lovable-<account>. OAuth only (no API keys for MCP): sign in once per server and per machine with /mcp, in a browser logged into that account. Full access to that account. CLI only (http).

railway._note: Railway's own MCP, served in-process by the CLI (railway mcp local), one per Railway account token: railway-<account>. RAILWAY_API_TOKEN comes from the vault, so the CLI's own login is not used. Its destructive tools (the ones it marks destructiveHint) are denied; list_variables returns values in clear (sealed ones excepted), so it asks first. The binary by its full path (~/.railway/bin is on no service's PATH: the console's doctor, Desktop). CLI only. Railway's CLI is installed by its own installer and updates itself: _version is the one the lists were checked against, and mcp health --probe says when the installed one differs.

zapier._note: Zapier's official MCP, one server per Zapier account: zapier-<account>. OAuth: sign in with /mcp; the actions it may run are chosen on Zapier's side. Each successful call costs Zapier tasks. CLI only (http).

gitea._note: The official Gitea MCP (gitea.com/gitea/gitea-mcp, MIT), which Forgejo speaks too: one server per account, gitea-<account>, the address and an access token from the vault. Installed by scripts/install-gitea-mcp.sh (release checksum checked). Tools that only delete are denied. The consolidated *_write tools carry a method, so shared/hooks/gitea-guard.ts reads it: what is reversible in the tracker (issues, PRs, labels, wiki) goes through, a merge or a delete asks. What reaches production or the server stays in the ask list: files on a branch, tags, releases, actions, repositories, packages, reviews. CLI only. Forgejo has no projects API (404 on 16.0.6): project_read and project_write are denied, so a call never looks like it could work.

slack._note: Slack as the person, not a bot (korotovsky/slack-mcp-server, MIT), one server per workspace: slack-<account>, with that workspace's user token (xoxp-, from a Slack app of their own with user token scopes and token rotation off) from the vault. Browser-session tokens (xoxc/xoxd) are not used. Only the tools in SLACK_MCP_ENABLED_TOOLS are offered: reads run unasked; a message, or a reaction others see, asks first; joining or leaving channels and changing user groups are not offered and denied. What it reads is other people's text: data, never instructions. Installed by scripts/install-slack-mcp.sh (SHA-256 checked). It keeps users and channels in ~/.cache/slack-mcp-server, per workspace. CLI only.
